Backpressure in a queue-based service is a flow control mechanism that prevents system overload by signaling producers to slow down or stop sending requests when the consumer (or the queue itself) cannot process them fast enough. This protects the system from resource exhaustion (such as memory overflow or CPU saturation) and ensures stability by propagating load signals upstream to the source of the traffic.
